Alzheimer's disease: A progressive, neurodegenerative disease characterized by loss of function and death of nerve cells in several areas of the brain leading to loss of cognitive function such as memory and language. (MONDO:0004975; MeSH:D000544; HP:0002511; NCIT:C2866; DOID:10652)
Tau load: The amount and anatomical distribution of tau pathology in tissue or in vivo, commonly quantified by neuropathologic staging or tau-PET burden. (EFO:0006797; https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37321820/)
Cognitive resilience: Ability to maintain the cognitive function despite the presence of neuropathological lesions, such as neurofibrillary tangles and Aβ. (doi:https://doi.org/10.1101/2025.01.13.632801)
Neuritic plaque load: The amount and anatomical distribution of neuritic amyloid-beta plaques (compact, dense-core deposits surrounded by dystrophic neurites) in tissue, quantified by neuropathologic staging or immunohistochemical scoring. (PMID:2011243)
Selective vulnerability: Different subpopulations of neurons across brain systems may vary in their vulnerability to dysfunction or death when exposed to specific pathological conditions or injuries. (DOI:10.1136/jnnp-2015-311321)
Diffuse plaque load: The amount and anatomical distribution of diffuse amyloid-beta plaques (loosely organized, non-compact deposits lacking dystrophic neurites) in tissue, quantified by neuropathologic staging or immunohistochemical scoring. (PMID:2011243)
Parkinson's disease: A progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by loss of dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra and the presence of Lewy bodies, causing motor symptoms (bradykinesia, rigidity, resting tremor) and various non-motor features. (MeSH:D010300; NCIT:C26845; MONDO:0005180; DOID:14330)
Neurogenesis: Formation of neurons which involves the differentation and division of stem cells in which one or bothy of the daughter cells become neurons. (MeSH:D055495; GO:0022008)
Aβ uptake (phagocytosis): Process by which cells (typically microglia or macrophages) engulf and internalize extracellular amyloid-beta peptide via phagocytosis or endocytosis, contributing to amyloid clearance. (DOI:10.1016/j.neuron.2014.01.030)
Aβ clearance: The process in which amyloid-beta is removed from extracellular brain regions by mechanisms involving cell surface receptors. (GO:0097242)
Amyloid load: The measured burden of amyloid-beta deposition (typically neuritic and diffuse plaques) in a brain region, quantified by immunohistochemistry, PET imaging, or histopathological scoring. (DOI:10.1002/ana.410340107)
Dementia with Lewy bodies: A neurodegenerative dementia characterized by α-synuclein-containing Lewy body pathology in cortical and subcortical regions, presenting with fluctuating cognition, visual hallucinations, parkinsonism, and REM sleep behaviour disorder. (MeSH:D020961; NCIT:C84826; HP:0100315; MONDO:0007488; EFO:0006792; DOID:12217)
Tau aggregation: Process where tau becomes abnormally phosphorylated and forms insoluble aggregates. (GO:1902988)
Cytokines: Non-antibody proteins secreted by inflammatory leukocytes and some non-leukocytic cells, that act as intercellular mediators. They differ from classical hormones in that they are produced by a number of tissue or cell types rather than by specialized glands. They generally act locally in a paracrine or autocrine rather than endocrine manner. (MeSH:D016207; EFO:0003786)
Astrogliosis: Reactive activation of astrocytes in response to CNS injury or disease, characterized by cellular hypertrophy, upregulation of GFAP and other intermediate filament proteins, and formation of glial scars. (MeSH:D005911)
BBB dysfunction: Impairment of the blood-brain barrier's selective permeability, characterized by loss of tight junction integrity, altered transporter function, and increased paracellular leak; implicated in Alzheimer's disease and other neurodegenerative conditions. (GO:1905605)
Microglia activation: A change in the morphology and behavior of a microglial cell resulting from exposure to a cytokine, chemokine, cellular ligand, or soluble factor. (GO:0001774)
Microgliosis: An accumulation of microglial cells in nervous tissue as a result of injury. (MP:0008918; NCIT:C120898)
Cognitive Dysfunction: A reduction from expected or prior performance in one or more cognitive domains, such as memory, attention, language, executive function, or visuospatial ability, whether measured cross-sectionally as impairment or longitudinally as decline. (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ols4/ontologies/hp/classes/http%253A%252F%252Fpurl.obolibrary.org%252Fobo%252FHP_0100543; HP:0001268; NCIT:C27101; DOID:0080832; NCIT:C116921; MeSH:D060825; NCIT:C46083)
Systemic inflammation: A phenotype representing systemic inflammatory status, often operationalized in population studies as a binary trait defined by elevated inflammatory biomarkers such as white blood cell count and/or high-sensitivity C-reactive protein. (EFO:0920000)
Neurodegeneration: Progressive loss of structure and function of neurons, including neuronal death, characteristic of neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer's, Parkinson's, and ALS. (MeSH:D019636; HP:0002180)
Astrocytes activation: A change in the morphology and behavior of an astrocyte resulting from exposure to a cytokine, chemokine, cellular ligand, or soluble factor. (GO:0048143)
Innate immune response: Innate immune responses are defense responses mediated by germline encoded components that directly recognize components of potential pathogens. (GO:0045087)
Neuroinflammation: Activation of the brain's innate immune system in response to an inflammatory challenge and is characterized by a host of cellular and molecular changes within the brain. (HP:0033429)
Oligodendrocytes maturation: The progression of oligodendrocyte-lineage cells from precursor or differentiating states to fully mature, myelinating oligodendrocytes. (GO:0048709)
Synaptic loss: Reduction or elimitation of synapses in the brain. (DOI https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-019-43076-y)
Tau degradation: The intracellular breakdown of tau protein via the ubiquitin-proteasome system or the autophagy-lysosome pathway, as distinct from extracellular disposal mechanisms (see Tau clearance). (DOI:10.1002/alz.70048)
Tau production: The generation and maintenance of tau protein abundance through transcriptional, chromatin-mediated, and post-translational mechanisms that support tau expression or stability, as distinct from its removal via degradative clearance pathways. (PMID:34127790)
Aβ accumulation: The build-up of amyloid-beta peptides in the brain, leading to plaque formation and neuronal toxicity in Alzheimer's disease. (doi.org/10.1038/aps.2017.28)
Excitatory neurons: A neuron whose synaptic output increases the likelihood of its postsynaptic targets firing action potentials. (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK11117/)
Interneurons: Most generally any neuron which is not motor or sensory. Interneurons may also refer to neurons whose axons remain within a particular brain region as contrasted with projection neurons which have axons projecting to other brain regions. (CL:0000099; MeSH:D007395; NCIT:C12625)
Microglia: The third type of glial cell, along with astrocytes and oligodendrocytes (which together form the macroglia). Microglia vary in appearance depending on developmental stage, functional state, and anatomical location; subtype terms include ramified, perivascular, ameboid, resting, and activated. Microglia clearly are capable of phagocytosis and play an important role in a wide spectrum of neuropathologies. They have also been suggested to act in several other roles, including in secretion (e.g., of cytokines and neural growth factors), in immunological processing (e.g., antigen presentation), and in central nervous system development and remodelling. (MeSH:D017628; BTO:0000078; CL:0000129; NCIT:C12616)
Astrocytes: A class of large neuroglial (macroglial) cells in the central nervous system - the largest and most numerous neuroglial cells in the brain and spinal cord. Astrocytes (from star cells) are irregularly shaped with many long processes, including those with end feet which form the glial (limiting) membrane and directly and indirectly contribute to the blood-brain barrier. They regulate the extracellular ionic and chemical environment, and reactive astrocytes (along with microglia) respond to injury. (MeSH:D001253; NCIT:C12477; CL:0000127)
Oligodendrocytes: A class of large neuroglial (macroglial) cells in the central nervous system. Oligodendroglia may be called interfascicular, perivascular, or perineuronal (not the same as satellite cells, perineuronal of ganglia) according to their location. They form the insulating myelin sheath of axons in the central nervous system. (MeSH:D009836; BTO:0000770; NCIT:C12618; CL:0000128)
Oligodendrocyte progenitor cells (OPCs): Neuroglial cells that first appear during mid-embryogenesis in the central nervous system of mammals and give rise to oligodendrocytes. Mitotically-active populations remain through late adulthood and are capable of regenerating myelin lost to disease or injury. (MeSH:D000073637; CL:0002453)
Immature neurons: A neuron in the central nervous system that is not committed to a differentiated fate, has not been newly derived from neurogenesis, and does not integrate into any circuit. (CL:4042028)
DG granule neurons: Glutamatergic granule cells of the hippocampal dentate gyrus, the principal input population of the hippocampal circuit and the population generated by adult hippocampal neurogenesis; annotated in Genedex from Mathys et al., Nature 2024 and Tosoni et al., Cell Stem Cell 2026 (PMID 39048816, 42034060). (CL:2000089; PMID:39048816; PMID:42034060)
Vascular cells: Broad category encompassing all cells forming or surrounding brain blood vessels, including endothelial cells, pericytes, vascular smooth muscle cells, and perivascular fibroblasts. Used when the underlying analysis pools multiple vascular cell types without further subdivision. (CL:4023072)
Homeostatic microglia: Microglia in baseline surveillant state, maintaining synapses and tissue homeostasis. (DOI:10.1016/j.neuron.2022.09.026)
AGBL1+/GPC5+ L5 excitatory neurons: Cortical excitatory neurons of layer 5 identified by co-expression of AGBL1 and GPC5; one of 76 cell types resolved in a single-nucleus atlas of six brain regions from 48 aged donors (Mathys et al., Nature 2024; PMID 39048816). (PMID:39048816)
CA1 pyramidal neurons: Glutamatergic pyramidal neurons of hippocampal subfield CA1, the principal output population of the hippocampal trisynaptic circuit; one of 76 cell types resolved in a single-nucleus atlas of six brain regions from 48 aged donors (Mathys et al., Nature 2024; PMID 39048816). (CL:0020072; PMID:39048816)
CA2/CA3 pyramidal neurons: Glutamatergic pyramidal neurons of hippocampal subfields CA2 and CA3, which form recurrent associative circuitry and project to CA1; one of 76 cell types resolved in a single-nucleus atlas of six brain regions from 48 aged donors (Mathys et al., Nature 2024; PMID 39048816). (PMID:39048816)
CBLN2+/LINC02306+ L2-3 excitatory neuron: Cortical excitatory neurons of layers 2-3 identified by co-expression of CBLN2 and LINC02306; one of 76 cell types resolved in a single-nucleus atlas of six brain regions from 48 aged donors (Mathys et al., Nature 2024; PMID 39048816). (PMID:39048816)
COBLL1+/UST+ excitatory neurons: Cortical excitatory neurons identified by co-expression of COBLL1 and UST; one of 76 cell types resolved in a single-nucleus atlas of six brain regions from 48 aged donors (Mathys et al., Nature 2024; PMID 39048816). (PMID:39048816)
DLC1+/SNTG2+ excitatory neurons: Cortical excitatory neurons identified by co-expression of DLC1 and SNTG2; one of 76 cell types resolved in a single-nucleus atlas of six brain regions from 48 aged donors (Mathys et al., Nature 2024; PMID 39048816). (PMID:39048816)
GRIK1+/CTXND1+ excitatory neurons (subic: Cortical excitatory neurons sampled in subiculum identified by co-expression of GRIK1 and CTXND1; one of 76 cell types resolved in a single-nucleus atlas of six brain regions from 48 aged donors (Mathys et al., Nature 2024; PMID 39048816). (PMID:39048816)
IT/Car3 L5-6 excitatory neurons: Intratelencephalic (IT) excitatory neurons of the Car3 subclass in cortical layers 5 and 6, projecting within the telencephalon including to claustral and insular targets; one of 76 cell types resolved in a single-nucleus atlas of six brain regions from 48 aged donors (Mathys et al., Nature 2024; PMID 39048816). (PMID:39048816)
L5 ET excitatory neurons: Layer 5 extratelencephalic (ET) projection neurons, large pyramidal cells whose axons leave the telencephalon for subcortical targets; one of 76 cell types resolved in a single-nucleus atlas of six brain regions from 48 aged donors (Mathys et al., Nature 2024; PMID 39048816). (CL:4023041; PMID:39048816)
L5/6 NP excitatory neurons: Near-projecting (NP) excitatory neurons of cortical layers 5 and 6, characterised by predominantly local and short-range cortical projections; one of 76 cell types resolved in a single-nucleus atlas of six brain regions from 48 aged donors (Mathys et al., Nature 2024; PMID 39048816). (CL:4030067; PMID:39048816)
L6 CT excitatory neurons: Layer 6 corticothalamic (CT) projection neurons, providing descending feedback from cortex to thalamus; one of 76 cell types resolved in a single-nucleus atlas of six brain regions from 48 aged donors (Mathys et al., Nature 2024; PMID 39048816). (CL:4023042; PMID:39048816)
L6b excitatory neurons: Excitatory neurons of cortical layer 6b, a thin deep sublayer derived from the embryonic subplate; one of 76 cell types resolved in a single-nucleus atlas of six brain regions from 48 aged donors (Mathys et al., Nature 2024; PMID 39048816). (CL:4023038; PMID:39048816)
NRGN+ excitatory neurons: Excitatory neurons distinguished by high neurogranin (NRGN) expression; one of 76 cell types resolved in a single-nucleus atlas of six brain regions from 48 aged donors (Mathys et al., Nature 2024; PMID 39048816). (PMID:39048816)
RELN+/COL5A2+ L2 excitatory neurons: Cortical excitatory neurons of layer 2 identified by co-expression of RELN and COL5A2; one of 76 cell types resolved in a single-nucleus atlas of six brain regions from 48 aged donors (Mathys et al., Nature 2024; PMID 39048816). (PMID:39048816)
RELN+/GPC5+ L2 excitatory neurons: Cortical excitatory neurons of layer 2 identified by co-expression of RELN and GPC5; one of 76 cell types resolved in a single-nucleus atlas of six brain regions from 48 aged donors (Mathys et al., Nature 2024; PMID 39048816). (PMID:39048816)
RORB+/CUX2+ L3-4 excitatory neurons: Cortical excitatory neurons of layers 3-4 identified by co-expression of RORB and CUX2; one of 76 cell types resolved in a single-nucleus atlas of six brain regions from 48 aged donors (Mathys et al., Nature 2024; PMID 39048816). (PMID:39048816)
RORB+/GABRG1+ L4-5 excitatory neurons: Cortical excitatory neurons of layers 4-5 identified by co-expression of RORB and GABRG1; one of 76 cell types resolved in a single-nucleus atlas of six brain regions from 48 aged donors (Mathys et al., Nature 2024; PMID 39048816). (PMID:39048816)
RORB+/IL1RAPL2+ L4-5 excitatory neurons: Cortical excitatory neurons of layers 4-5 identified by co-expression of RORB and IL1RAPL2; one of 76 cell types resolved in a single-nucleus atlas of six brain regions from 48 aged donors (Mathys et al., Nature 2024; PMID 39048816). (PMID:39048816)
RORB+/LINC02196+ L5-6 excitatory neurons: Cortical excitatory neurons of layers 5-6 identified by co-expression of RORB and LINC02196; one of 76 cell types resolved in a single-nucleus atlas of six brain regions from 48 aged donors (Mathys et al., Nature 2024; PMID 39048816). (PMID:39048816)
RORB+/PLCH1+ L3-5 excitatory neurons: Cortical excitatory neurons of layers 3-5 identified by co-expression of RORB and PLCH1; one of 76 cell types resolved in a single-nucleus atlas of six brain regions from 48 aged donors (Mathys et al., Nature 2024; PMID 39048816). (PMID:39048816)
THEMIS+/NFIA+ L6 excitatory neurons: Cortical excitatory neurons of layer 6 identified by co-expression of THEMIS and NFIA; one of 76 cell types resolved in a single-nucleus atlas of six brain regions from 48 aged donors (Mathys et al., Nature 2024; PMID 39048816). (PMID:39048816)
TOX3+/INO80D+ excitatory neurons: Cortical excitatory neurons identified by co-expression of TOX3 and INO80D; one of 76 cell types resolved in a single-nucleus atlas of six brain regions from 48 aged donors (Mathys et al., Nature 2024; PMID 39048816). (PMID:39048816)
TOX3+/TTC6+ excitatory neurons: Cortical excitatory neurons identified by co-expression of TOX3 and TTC6; one of 76 cell types resolved in a single-nucleus atlas of six brain regions from 48 aged donors (Mathys et al., Nature 2024; PMID 39048816). (PMID:39048816)
TRPC6+/ANO2+ excitatory neurons: Cortical excitatory neurons identified by co-expression of TRPC6 and ANO2; one of 76 cell types resolved in a single-nucleus atlas of six brain regions from 48 aged donors (Mathys et al., Nature 2024; PMID 39048816). (PMID:39048816)
ZNF385D+/COL24A1+ excitatory neurons: Cortical excitatory neurons identified by co-expression of ZNF385D and COL24A1; one of 76 cell types resolved in a single-nucleus atlas of six brain regions from 48 aged donors (Mathys et al., Nature 2024; PMID 39048816). (PMID:39048816)
CBLN2+/LINC00507+ L2-3 excitatory neuron: Cortical excitatory neurons of layers 2-3 identified by co-expression of CBLN2 and LINC00507; resolved by single-nucleus RNA sequencing with neuropathological phenotyping of tau-associated neuronal vulnerability (Lin et al., Cell Reports 2025; PMID 40448997). This population was validated by multiplexed immunohistochemistry and in situ hybridisation for CBLN2 and LINC00507 as especially vulnerable to tau pathology. (PMID:40448997)
Endothelial cells: Highly specialized epithelial-like cells lining heart, blood and lymphatic vessels, forming the endothelium. (MeSH:D042783; NCIT:C12865; CL:0000115)
Interneurons SST9: Cortical interneuron supertype SST_9 (somatostatin-expressing); a supertype of the SEA-AD middle temporal gyrus taxonomy, mapped to the BRAIN Initiative human cortical reference atlas (Gabitto et al., Nature Neuroscience 2024; PMID 39402379). Somatostatin-expressing inhibitory neurons decline in the early phase of the disease pseudoprogression trajectory reported in that study. (PMID:39402379)
Perivascular cells: A cell that is adjacent to a vessel. A perivascular cell plays a crucial role in maintaining vascular function and tissue homeostasis. This cell type regulates vessel integrity and flow dynamics. (CL:4033054)
Amyloid-associated microglia: A phagocytic, activated microglia state described in human Alzheimer's disease brain tissue (subclusters 7, 9, and 10 of Gerrits et al. 2021), sharing features with the DAM/ARM profile from amyloid mouse models; abundance correlates strongly with tissue amyloid-beta load. (https://doi.org/10.1007/s00401-021-02263-w)
PROX1+/DLX6-AS1+ VIP interneurons: VIP-expressing cortical interneurons identified by co-expression of PROX1 and DLX6-AS1; resolved by single-nucleus RNA sequencing with neuropathological phenotyping of tau-associated neuronal vulnerability (Lin et al., Cell Reports 2025; PMID 40448997). (PMID:40448997)
Tau-associated microglia: A partially homeostatic, neuron-associated microglia state described in human Alzheimer's disease brain tissue (subclusters 2, 3, and 6 of Gerrits et al. 2021), enriched for synapse organisation and axonogenesis genes (e.g. GRID2); abundance correlates strongly with tissue phospho-tau load. (https://doi.org/10.1007/s00401-021-02263-w)
COL25A1+/SEMA3D+ excitatory neurons: Cortical excitatory neurons identified by co-expression of COL25A1 and SEMA3D; one of 76 cell types resolved in a single-nucleus atlas of six brain regions from 48 aged donors (Mathys et al., Nature 2024; PMID 39048816). (PMID:39048816)
Ribosome biogenesis microglia: A translation/ribosome-assembly state with nucleolar/ribosome-biogenesis signatures. (DOI:10.1016/j.cell.2023.08.037)
SEMA3E+/ADAMTSL1+ L6 corticothalamic exc: Corticothalamic excitatory neurons of layer 6 identified by co-expression of SEMA3E and ADAMTSL1; resolved by single-nucleus RNA sequencing with neuropathological phenotyping of tau-associated neuronal vulnerability (Lin et al., Cell Reports 2025; PMID 40448997). (PMID:40448997)
THEMIS+/CBLN2+ L6 excitatory neurons: Cortical excitatory neurons of layer 6 identified by co-expression of THEMIS and CBLN2; resolved by single-nucleus RNA sequencing with neuropathological phenotyping of tau-associated neuronal vulnerability (Lin et al., Cell Reports 2025; PMID 40448997). (PMID:40448997)
Astrocytes subtype2: Astrocyte transcriptomic subtype 2; a supertype of the SEA-AD middle temporal gyrus taxonomy, mapped to the BRAIN Initiative human cortical reference atlas (Gabitto et al., Nature Neuroscience 2024; PMID 39402379). (PMID:39402379)
Brain immune cells: CNS-resident immune cells that continuously surveys the brain environment and carry out immune, phagocytic, and homeostatic functions within the central nervous system. (DOI:10.1016/j.immuni.2021.08.010)
Cycling microglia: A proliferative/cell-cycle state marked by expression of mitotic machinery (e.g., MKI67/TOP2A-like programs). (DOI:10.1016/j.cell.2023.08.037)
Excitatory neurons L6CT_2: Cortical excitatory neuron supertype L6CT_2 (L6 corticothalamic); a supertype of the SEA-AD middle temporal gyrus taxonomy, mapped to the BRAIN Initiative human cortical reference atlas (Gabitto et al., Nature Neuroscience 2024; PMID 39402379). (PMID:39402379)
FBXL7+/KIT+ LAMP5 interneurons: LAMP5-expressing cortical interneurons identified by co-expression of FBXL7 and KIT; resolved by single-nucleus RNA sequencing with neuropathological phenotyping of tau-associated neuronal vulnerability (Lin et al., Cell Reports 2025; PMID 40448997). (PMID:40448997)
LRRK1+/AC016687.2+ L5 excitatory neurons: Cortical excitatory neurons of layer 5 identified by co-expression of LRRK1 and AC016687.2; resolved by single-nucleus RNA sequencing with neuropathological phenotyping of tau-associated neuronal vulnerability (Lin et al., Cell Reports 2025; PMID 40448997). (PMID:40448997)
Microglia PVM3: Perivascular macrophage (PVM) supertype 3; a supertype of the SEA-AD middle temporal gyrus taxonomy, mapped to the BRAIN Initiative human cortical reference atlas (Gabitto et al., Nature Neuroscience 2024; PMID 39402379). (PMID:39402379)
Pericytes: Unique slender cells with multiple processes extending along the capillary vessel axis and encircling the vascular wall, also called mural cells. Pericytes are imbedded in the basement membrane shared with the endothelial cells of the vessel. Pericytes are important in maintaining vessel integrity, angiogenesis, and vascular remodeling. (MeSH:D020286; NCIT:C12656; CL:0000669)
POSTN+/AC110023.1+ L6 CAR3 excitatory ne: CAR3 excitatory neurons of layer 6 identified by co-expression of POSTN and AC110023.1; resolved by single-nucleus RNA sequencing with neuropathological phenotyping of tau-associated neuronal vulnerability (Lin et al., Cell Reports 2025; PMID 40448997). (PMID:40448997)
Stress microglia: A cell-stress response state (heat-shock/oxidative-stress pathways), increased with pathology and reduced after plaque-targeting immunisation in external validation. (DOI:10.1016/j.cell.2023.08.037)
Antiviral microglia: Microglia characterised by a type-I interferon/antiviral gene program (interferon-stimulated genes such as IFITM/ISG/OAS/MX), indicating antiviral defence signalling. (DOI:10.1016/j.cell.2023.08.037)
CNR1+/SGO1-AS1+ SNCG interneurons: SNCG-expressing cortical interneurons identified by co-expression of CNR1 and SGO1-AS1; resolved by single-nucleus RNA sequencing with neuropathological phenotyping of tau-associated neuronal vulnerability (Lin et al., Cell Reports 2025; PMID 40448997). (PMID:40448997)
Disease associated microglia (DAM): Microglia characterised by low expression of homeostatic genes and with upregulated genes involved in neurodegenerative disease, like AD. (DOI:10.1016/j.cell.2017.05.018)
Excitatory neurons L23IT_3: Cortical excitatory neuron supertype L23IT_3 (L2/3 intratelencephalic); a supertype of the SEA-AD middle temporal gyrus taxonomy, mapped to the BRAIN Initiative human cortical reference atlas (Gabitto et al., Nature Neuroscience 2024; PMID 39402379). (PMID:39402379)
Excitatory neurons L23IT_6: Cortical excitatory neuron supertype L23IT_6 (L2/3 intratelencephalic); a supertype of the SEA-AD middle temporal gyrus taxonomy, mapped to the BRAIN Initiative human cortical reference atlas (Gabitto et al., Nature Neuroscience 2024; PMID 39402379). (PMID:39402379)
Excitatory neurons L23IT_8: Cortical excitatory neuron supertype L23IT_8 (L2/3 intratelencephalic); a supertype of the SEA-AD middle temporal gyrus taxonomy, mapped to the BRAIN Initiative human cortical reference atlas (Gabitto et al., Nature Neuroscience 2024; PMID 39402379). (PMID:39402379)
Excitatory neurons L56NP_2: Cortical excitatory neuron supertype L56NP_2 (L5/6 near-projecting); a supertype of the SEA-AD middle temporal gyrus taxonomy, mapped to the BRAIN Initiative human cortical reference atlas (Gabitto et al., Nature Neuroscience 2024; PMID 39402379). (PMID:39402379)
Excitatory neurons L5IT_7: Cortical excitatory neuron supertype L5IT_7 (L5 intratelencephalic); a supertype of the SEA-AD middle temporal gyrus taxonomy, mapped to the BRAIN Initiative human cortical reference atlas (Gabitto et al., Nature Neuroscience 2024; PMID 39402379). (PMID:39402379)
Glycolytic microglia: A metabolic reprogramming state enriched for glycolysis and related energy-pathway genes, consistent with inflammatory activation. (DOI:10.1016/j.cell.2023.08.037)
HTR2C+/NPSR1-AS1+ L5-6 near-projecting e: Near-projecting excitatory neurons of layers 5-6 identified by co-expression of HTR2C and NPSR1-AS1; resolved by single-nucleus RNA sequencing with neuropathological phenotyping of tau-associated neuronal vulnerability (Lin et al., Cell Reports 2025; PMID 40448997). (PMID:40448997)
Inflammatory microglia high: A subtype or subset of inflammatory microglia exhibiting the highest levels of inflammatory gene expression among the inflammatory cluster in that study. (DOI:10.1016/j.cell.2023.08.037)
Inflammatory microglia low: A subtype of inflammatory microglia with the lowest (but still elevated relative to homeostatic) expression of inflammation-associated genes within the inflammatory cluster. (DOI:10.1016/j.cell.2023.08.037)
Inflammatory microglia medium: A subtype of inflammatory microglia with intermediate expression levels of inflammatory genes (moderate activation) relative to high and low subtypes. (DOI:10.1016/j.cell.2023.08.037)
Interneurons SST2: Cortical interneuron supertype SST_2 (somatostatin-expressing); a supertype of the SEA-AD middle temporal gyrus taxonomy, mapped to the BRAIN Initiative human cortical reference atlas (Gabitto et al., Nature Neuroscience 2024; PMID 39402379). Somatostatin-expressing inhibitory neurons decline in the early phase of the disease pseudoprogression trajectory reported in that study. (PMID:39402379)
Interneurons SST3: Cortical interneuron supertype SST_3 (somatostatin-expressing); a supertype of the SEA-AD middle temporal gyrus taxonomy, mapped to the BRAIN Initiative human cortical reference atlas (Gabitto et al., Nature Neuroscience 2024; PMID 39402379). Somatostatin-expressing inhibitory neurons decline in the early phase of the disease pseudoprogression trajectory reported in that study. (PMID:39402379)
Lipid processing microglia: A lipid/cholesterol handling state enriched for lipid metabolism and transport programs (e.g., APOE/LPL/PPARG-type modules); expanded in AD relative to controls. (DOI:10.1016/j.cell.2023.08.037)
Macrophages: Long-lived phagocytic cells derived from monocytes or embryonic precursors; key effectors of innate immunity. (MeSH:D008264; CL:0000235; NCIT:C12558)
Neuronal surveillance microglia: A surveillant/homeostatic-adjacent state maintaining interaction with neuronal elements; defined by high expression of homeostatic/sensome receptors (e.g., P2RY12/CX3CR1 backbone). (DOI:10.1016/j.cell.2023.08.037)
NXPH1+/RNF220+ excitatory neurons: Cortical excitatory neurons identified by co-expression of NXPH1 and RNF220; one of 76 cell types resolved in a single-nucleus atlas of six brain regions from 48 aged donors (Mathys et al., Nature 2024; PMID 39048816). (PMID:39048816)
Phagocytic microglia: A phagocytosis/lysosome-enriched state (endolysosomal and engulfment programs) linked to debris/synapse/aggregate clearance. (DOI:10.1016/j.cell.2023.08.037)
SLC9A9+/TMEM132C+ chandelier interneuron: Chandelier interneurons identified by co-expression of SLC9A9 and TMEM132C; resolved by single-nucleus RNA sequencing with neuropathological phenotyping of tau-associated neuronal vulnerability (Lin et al., Cell Reports 2025; PMID 40448997). (PMID:40448997)
SOX6+/KIF26B+ SST interneurons: Somatostatin-expressing cortical interneurons identified by co-expression of SOX6 and KIF26B; resolved by single-nucleus RNA sequencing with neuropathological phenotyping of tau-associated neuronal vulnerability (Lin et al., Cell Reports 2025; PMID 40448997). (PMID:40448997)
VAT1L+/ERBB4+ excitatory neurons: Cortical excitatory neurons identified by co-expression of VAT1L and ERBB4; one of 76 cell types resolved in a single-nucleus atlas of six brain regions from 48 aged donors (Mathys et al., Nature 2024; PMID 39048816). (PMID:39048816)

Brain: The brain is the center of the nervous system in all vertebrate, and most invertebrate, animals. Some primitive animals such as jellyfish and starfish have a decentralized nervous system without a brain, while sponges lack any nervous system at all. In vertebrates, the brain is located in the head, protected by the skull and close to the primary sensory apparatus of vision, hearing, balance, taste, and smell[WP]. (UBERON:0000955; NCIT:C12439; MeSH:D001921)
Hippocampus: A part of the brain consisting of a three layered cortex located in the forebrain bordering the medial surface of the lateral ventricle. The term hippocampus is often used synonymously with hippocampal formation which consists of the hippocampus proper or Cornu Ammonis, the dentate gyrus and the subiculum. (UBERON:0002421; NCIT:C12444; MeSH:D006624)
Temporal Cortex: Gray matter of the temporal region of the neocortex, located in the temporal lobe in gyrencephalic animals. (UBERON:0016538; NCIT:C177768)
Entorhinal Cortex: Component of the temporal lobe on the mesial surface. The rostral and caudal boundaries of the entorhinal cortex are the rostral end of the collateral sulcus and the caudal end of the amygdala respectively. The medial boundary is the medial aspect of the temporal lobe and the lateral boundary is the collateral sulcus. (DK). (UBERON:0002728; NCIT:C97338; MeSH:D018728)
Prefrontal Cortex: The anterior part of the frontal lobes of the brain, lying in front of the motor and premotor areas. This brain region has been implicated in planning complex cognitive behaviors, personality expression, decision making and moderating correct social behavior. The basic activity of this brain region is considered to be orchestration of thoughts and actions in accordance with internal goals. The most typical psychological term for functions carried out by the pre-frontal cortex area is executive function. Executive function relates to abilities to differentiate among conflicting thoughts, determine good and bad, better and best, same and different, future consequences of current activities, working toward a defined goal, prediction of outcomes, expectation based on actions, and social 'control' (the ability to suppress urges that, if not suppressed, could lead to socially-unacceptable outcomes). Many authors have indicated an integral link between a person's personality and the functions of the prefrontal cortex. - definition adapted from Wikipedia. (UBERON:0000451; MeSH:D017397; NCIT:C154779)
Neocortex: The six-layered portion of the cerebral cortex that forms the majority of the human cortical surface, spanning frontal, parietal, temporal and occipital primary and association areas; used where a study pools cortical samples without specifying a single region. (UBERON:0001950; MeSH:D019579; BTO:0000920)
Angular Gyrus: A gyrus of the inferior parietal lobule, posterior to the supramarginal gyrus, involved in semantic processing, reading and number processing; a region sampled in studies of the spatiotemporal progression of Alzheimer's disease pathology. (UBERON:0002686; NCIT:C32077; FMA:61898; SNOMEDCT:279186009; PMID:31551718)
Cingulate Cortex: The cingulate cortex is a part of the brain situated in the medial aspect of the cortex. It is extended from the corpus callosum below to the cingulate sulcus above, at least anteriorly. [WP,unvetted]. (UBERON:0003027; NCIT:C52713)
Midbrain: The middle portion of the brainstem containing the substantia nigra (dopaminergic neurons), red nucleus, and cerebral peduncles; central to motor control and reward processing and the primary site of dopaminergic neurodegeneration in Parkinson's disease. (MeSH:D008636; UBERON:0001891; NCIT:C12510)
Thalamus: Subcortical brain region consisting of paired gray matter bodies in the dorsal diencephalon and forming part of the lateral wall of the third ventricle of the brain. The thalamus represents the major portion of the diencephalon and is commonly divided into cellular aggregates known as nuclear groups.(MeSH). The dorsal topographic division of the interbrain. The macrodissected adult human thalamus was clearly illustrated by Vesalius in 1543 and the term as defined here was introduced by His in 1893. It includes the traditional epithalamus, dorsal thalamus, and ventral thalamus of Herrick (1910, pp. 494, 498). Also see Kuhlenbeck (1927, Ch. 9) and Jones (1985, p. 87). (UBERON:0001897; MeSH:D013788; NCIT:C12459)
Inferior Temporal Gyrus: Component of the temporal lobe, lateral aspect. The rostral boundary is the rostral extent of the inferior temporal sulcus whereas the caudal boundary is designated as the temporo-occipital incisure on the cortical surface. The occipitotemporal sulcus is the medial boundary and the inferior temporal sulcus is the lateral boundary (Christine Fennema-Notestine). (UBERON:0002751; BTO:0006175; NCIT:C32791)
Superior Frontal Gyrus: Component of the frontal lobe, lateral aspect. The rostral boundary is the first appearance of the superior frontal sulcus whereas the caudal boundary is the midpoint of the paracentral sulcus on the 'inflated' surface. The medial and lateral boundaries are the medial aspect of the frontal lobe and the superior frontal sulcus respectively (Christine Fennema-Notestine). (UBERON:0002661; NCIT:C33674)
Frontal Cortex: Anterior portion of the neocortex, lying anterior to the central sulcus in humans. It is bounded by the parietal cortex posteriorly and the temporal cortex laterally. (UBERON:0001870)
Secondary Visual Cortex: A functional part of the visual cortex that plays a crucial role in the integration of information from various visual modalities and contribute to higher-order visual functions, including colour, object recognition and spatial awareness. (UBERON:0022232)
Primary Visual Cortex: The visual area of the brain that is specialized for processing information about static and moving objects. The primary visual cortex, which is defined by its function or stage in the visual system, is approximately equivalent to the striate cortex, also known as Brodmann area 17, which is defined by its anatomical location. (UBERON:0002436; MeSH:D000087642; NCIT:C97340)
Cerebral Cortex: The thin layer of gray matter on the surface of the cerebral hemisphere that develops from the telencephalon. It consists of the neocortex (6 layered cortex or isocortex), the hippocampal formation and the olfactory cortex. (UBERON:0000956; MeSH:D002540)
Blood: A fluid that is composed of blood plasma and erythrocytes. (UBERON:0000178; NCIT:C12434; MeSH:D001769)
Parietal Cortex: Gray matter of the parietal region of the neocortex, located in the parietal lobe of gyrencephalic animals. It is continuous anteriorly with the frontal cortex, posteriorly with the occipital cortex and medially with the insular cortex and with the temporal cortex on the posterior/inferior border. (UBERON:0016530; NCIT:C177764)
Prefrontal Cortex, Layer 2-3: Superficial cortico-cortical projection layers of the prefrontal cortex (upper part of layer 2 through layer 3), enriched in intratelencephalic (IT) excitatory neurons with local and long-range corticocortical connections. (DOI:10.1038/s41586-021-03950-0)
Prefrontal Cortex, Layer 2-4: Superficial to mid prefrontal cortical layers (2–4), spanning small pyramidal and stellate cortico-cortical projection neurons and layer 4 granular input neurons. (DOI:10.1038/s41586-021-03950-0)
Prefrontal Cortex, Layer 4-5: Mid prefrontal cortical layers (4–5) encompassing granular input layer 4 and pyramidal projection layer 5, including corticothalamic and pyramidal tract subtypes. (DOI:10.1038/s41586-021-03950-0)
Prefrontal Cortex, Layer 5: Prefrontal cortical layer 5, populated by large pyramidal projection neurons including intratelencephalic (IT), pyramidal tract (PT), and extratelencephalic subtypes. (DOI:10.1038/s41586-021-03950-0)
Prefrontal Cortex, Layer 5-6: Deep prefrontal cortical layers (5–6) containing pyramidal projection neurons of the corticofugal output, including corticothalamic (CT) and pyramidal-tract subtypes. (DOI:10.1038/s41586-021-03950-0)
SH-SY5Y neuroblastoma cell line: A human neuroblastoma-derived cell line widely used as an in vitro neuronal model in Alzheimer's and Parkinson's disease research; not primary or patient-derived tissue. (Cellosaurus:CVCL_0019; PMID:34127790)
Choroid Plexus: A network formed by blood vessels and the tela choroidea which secretes CSF into the ventricular spaces. (UBERON:0001886; NCIT:C12694; MeSH:D002831)
Abeta accumulation: The build-up of amyloid-beta peptides in the brain, leading to plaque formation and neuronal toxicity in Alzheimer's disease. (doi.org/10.1038/aps.2017.28)
Aging microglia: A microglial subtype defined by a transcriptomic signature enriched in ageing-associated genes (e.g. those upregulated with chronological age), reflecting age-related changes in microglial function and gene expression. (DOI:10.1038/s41467-020-19737-2)
Ependymal_cells: Ciliated epithelial cells lining the cerebral ventricles and central canal, contributing to cerebrospinal fluid movement and to the ventricular barrier; annotated in Genedex from Mathys et al., Nature 2024 and Smajić et al., Brain 2022 (PMID 39048816, 34919646).
Interneurons Pvallb_12: Cortical interneuron supertype Pvalb_12 (parvalbumin-expressing); a supertype of the SEA-AD middle temporal gyrus taxonomy, mapped to the BRAIN Initiative human cortical reference atlas (Gabitto et al., Nature Neuroscience 2024; PMID 39402379). Parvalbumin- and VIP-expressing inhibitory neuron subtypes decline in the later phase of that trajectory.
Interneurons Pvallb_14: Cortical interneuron supertype Pvalb_14 (parvalbumin-expressing); a supertype of the SEA-AD middle temporal gyrus taxonomy, mapped to the BRAIN Initiative human cortical reference atlas (Gabitto et al., Nature Neuroscience 2024; PMID 39402379). Parvalbumin- and VIP-expressing inhibitory neuron subtypes decline in the later phase of that trajectory.
Interneurons Pvallb_3: Cortical interneuron supertype Pvalb_3 (parvalbumin-expressing); a supertype of the SEA-AD middle temporal gyrus taxonomy, mapped to the BRAIN Initiative human cortical reference atlas (Gabitto et al., Nature Neuroscience 2024; PMID 39402379). Parvalbumin- and VIP-expressing inhibitory neuron subtypes decline in the later phase of that trajectory.
Interneurons Pvallb_8: Cortical interneuron supertype Pvalb_8 (parvalbumin-expressing); a supertype of the SEA-AD middle temporal gyrus taxonomy, mapped to the BRAIN Initiative human cortical reference atlas (Gabitto et al., Nature Neuroscience 2024; PMID 39402379). Parvalbumin- and VIP-expressing inhibitory neuron subtypes decline in the later phase of that trajectory.
ATP8B1+ excitatory neurons: Excitatory neurons of the entorhinal cortex identified by expression of ATP8B1 (subcluster Exc3); resolved by multiregional single-nucleus RNA sequencing of ROSMAP donors classified as Alzheimer's disease, resilient or control (Castanho et al., Molecular Neurodegeneration 2025; PMID 41035073). A resilience-associated subtype whose proportion increased in resilient brains. (PMID:41035073)
Cognitive dysfunction: A reduction from expected or prior performance in one or more cognitive domains, such as memory, attention, language, executive function, or visuospatial ability, whether measured cross-sectionally as impairment or longitudinally as decline. (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ols4/ontologies/hp/classes/http%253A%252F%252Fpurl.obolibrary.org%252Fobo%252FHP_0100543; HP:0001268; NCIT:C27101; DOID:0080832; NCIT:C116921; MeSH:D060825; NCIT:C46083)
MEF2C+/ATP8B1+/RELN+ excitatory neurons: Excitatory neurons of the entorhinal cortex identified by co-expression of MEF2C, ATP8B1 and RELN (subcluster Exc2); resolved by multiregional single-nucleus RNA sequencing of ROSMAP donors classified as Alzheimer's disease, resilient or control (Castanho et al., Molecular Neurodegeneration 2025; PMID 41035073). A resilience-associated subtype whose proportion increased in resilient brains. (PMID:41035073)
MEF2C+/RELN+ excitatory neurons: Excitatory neurons of the entorhinal cortex identified by co-expression of MEF2C and RELN (subcluster Exc5); resolved by multiregional single-nucleus RNA sequencing of ROSMAP donors classified as Alzheimer's disease, resilient or control (Castanho et al., Molecular Neurodegeneration 2025; PMID 41035073). A resilience-associated subtype whose proportion increased in resilient brains. (PMID:41035073)
NK cells (Natural killer): Innate lymphoid cells with cytotoxic activity against virus-infected and transformed cells, independent of antigen specificity. (MeSH:D007694; CL:0000623; NCIT:C12536)
RBFOX1+/KIF26B+ SST interneurons: Somatostatin-expressing (SST+) inhibitory interneurons of the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex identified by co-expression of RBFOX1 and KIF26B (subcluster Inh1); resolved by multiregional single-nucleus RNA sequencing of ROSMAP donors classified as Alzheimer's disease, resilient or control (Castanho et al., Molecular Neurodegeneration 2025; PMID 41035073). A vulnerable subtype whose proportion decreased in Alzheimer's disease but not in resilient brains. (PMID:41035073)
